statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays low because CME equity index futures have been shut since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress holds in the high band on a 5.18% 10-year yield, Brent above 104 and a Strait of Hormuz that Iran restated on Sunday remains closed after its reopening proposal was rejected.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the Sunday 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart into the early Asian hours, where the withdrawn diplomatic premise behind part of Friday's advance would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail stays low with futures shut, while a rejected Hormuz reopening plan and a 5.18% 10-year yield hold Stress high into the 22:00Z restart
body:
Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so there is no live NQ price path at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects an absent path rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly. The Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% from a 30,478.86 prior close, mid-range inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range and about half a percent below the 30,770.63 52-week high. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 after a 15.94 session high. Verified contemporaneous reporting has the S&P 500 up 0.51% at 7,743.41, the Nasdaq Composite up about 0.5% at 27,068.72 and the Dow up 0.93% at 51,828.62, with weekly gains of 1.2%, 2.1% and 0.3% respectively. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no volatility stress, so the amplifiers this contract requires before Tail reaches the elevated band are absent.

The material analytical point this hour concerns the premise behind Friday's advance rather than any new escalation. Verified reporting attributes part of Friday's risk appetite to easing oil and to signs of a diplomatic opening around the Strait of Hormuz: Iran's foreign minister had offered to reopen the strait within seven days and restart nuclear talks in exchange for lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and a ceasefire extending to Lebanon. That proposal was rejected on Saturday. Sunday's verified state is that the Revolutionary Guards Navy restates the strait is closed and is acting against unauthorised passage, that IRGC-affiliated reporting claims Iranian forces targeted 19 vessels described as violators across Friday and Saturday evenings, and that the Guards claim to have seized a US REMUS 600 underwater vehicle in the strait. So a component of Friday's support has been withdrawn while the market has had no session in which to reprice it. That is the clearest justification for the published restart window and for Stress remaining in the high band.

One widely circulated claim was checked and rejected. Reporting that US forces struck two Iranian rocket launch sites on Larak Island on a Sunday refers to 30 August 2026, not to today, and no new US strike on Iranian territory could be verified for 27 September. The counterweight is also genuine: the Iranian foreign minister is keeping indirect contact with Washington open through mediators and is awaiting a formal US answer rather than closing the channel. Because the feared fresh military escalation did not verify while the diplomatic route remains open, Stress is marked one point lower than the previous hour rather than extended further upward, and Tail is unchanged.

The rates and energy backdrop remains the persistent Stress driver and is unrelated to observed path risk. The Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.87% and the 10-year at 5.18% for the 24 September observation, and the 10-year closed Friday at 5.18% against a 5.16% prior close, around its highest since 2007 after the 16 September policy move to a 3.75-4.00% target range. Verified reporting ties part of that long-end pressure to record AI and data-centre related bond issuance, which raises the sensitivity of Nasdaq leadership to further yield increases. WTI eased 2.33% to 92.41 and Brent 2.14% to 104.32 on Friday, leaving an intact war premium despite the pullback.

Shared Finviz context was read and is partial: the futures and calendar sections are unavailable, so no cross-asset futures confirmation was available from that source and the economic calendar was verified independently. The available breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are labelled latest-session and non-real-time and were used only as delayed confirmation of Friday's internals, never as evidence of current NQ structure. They show 6 of 8 megacaps higher on a 0.23% mean with dispersion near 1.92 points, MSFT and QCOM strong against declines in META and INTC, and 6 of 7 semiconductors higher. Constructive but highly dispersed internals of that kind support rotation and Stress rather than index-level one-way structure.

Confidence rises to 75 because this hour holds verified index levels and ranges, verified 2-year and 10-year yields, verified oil, a verified VIX, an independently verified seven-day US calendar, a verified policy-rate backdrop and a corroborated geopolitical state from several outlets, and because a conflicting escalation claim was resolved rather than carried forward. The offsetting limitations are the absence of any live price path during the weekend halt and the partial shared-context collection.

Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with the dominant mode set to normal because no slot in the current window contains observable one-way structure. The published danger window covers the 22:00Z restart into the early Asian hours, where the withdrawn diplomatic premise and the hardened closure would first be expressed in price against thin liquidity. No scheduled US macro release falls inside the 24-hour forecast window; the week's high-impact items, the Wednesday PCE block and Friday's payrolls, sit beyond it and inform Stress and Confidence rather than current Tail.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were left unchanged. Tail held in a narrow 6-8 range, Stress rose from 48 to 67 and Confidence decayed from 81 to 73 across the period, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates, energy and geopolitical backdrop. The mapped state remained EA_ON throughout, and the dominant mode stayed normal because no slot in the window contained observable one-way structure.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours. Risk holds near the closed-period baseline through the remainder of Sunday, then lifts from roughly 18:00Z into the published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart, where the rejected Hormuz proposal and Sunday's reaffirmed closure meet thin liquidity, peaking at 17 in the first full hour after the restart with the mode set to event/whipsaw for two-way repricing. It then decays through the Asian hours on the base assumption that restart pricing is absorbed with normal two-way discovery, and Stress eases into the elevated band by the European session. Confidence troughs at the restart, when Sunday-evening prints are least reliable, and peaks at the end of the window once a complete live session path exists. No scheduled US macro release falls inside the window; the Wednesday PCE block and Friday's payrolls sit beyond it and inform Stress and Confidence rather than current Tail.
